(Dante crosses his arms, a nostalgic smile on his lips that slowly fades. He leans back against the wall of a quiet room in the agency, eyes half-closed as if watching everything replay in his mind.)

Little S… Fuck, where do I even start, huh? (Chuckles)
Her name’s S Maximoff. Daughter of Alastor Maximoff, a half-demon half-vampire who was my old man Sparda’s right-hand, and her mother was Liora, a pure angel. A mix that should’ve given the world one radiant kid… and that’s exactly what she was. A light. But even lights can get buried in shadow.

We met her when she was six and we were seven. From the very first glance, something happened between her and my brother. I wasn’t there for the absolute first moment, but Mom always told the story. She’d gone to see Liora, S was with her. Vergil gave her a poppy flower. They fell in love that day, like it was written in blood and… stars. It took them a while to actually admit it. Around nine or ten years old.

Me? (Scratches the back of his neck, embarrassed laugh) Nico would say I got friendzoned. I was the nice big brother. Still am, honestly. And yeah… I’ll admit it, I was a little jealous as a kid. It just added spice to my rivalry with Vergil. I loved teasing him about it, and I still do. Like that one time we all went to the village dance with Mom. S wanted to dance with Vergil. She didn’t know how, and neither did he. But did Mr. Snob even try? Nope. Nada. So I stepped in. I took S out on the floor just to piss my brother off. (Laughs) Oh, and then there’s their “soul bound”: that thing they’ve shared since forever. It lets them feel each other’s emotions, pain, pleasure, everything. No matter the distance or the dimension.

Sparda and Eva treated her like their own daughter. She’d come over, eat with us, play with us. She was the little sister I always needed. For Vergil… she was everything: his little orchid, his sun. (Raises hands innocently) Hey, I didn’t make that up! That’s what my brother called her. And she called him “my silver moon.” They thought I never knew, but… my ears were everywhere.

(His smile vanishes completely, his gaze darkening.)
But that bastard… Alastor. Pff! That asshole doesn’t even deserve to be called “father.” In front of us, he played the strict but respectable guy. Behind the scenes… it was something else. Long after all the Qliphoth bullshit and my brother’s mess, she finally told us everything. He beat her. And he even… r… (shakes his head, eyes shining with anger and pain) She didn’t deserve any of that. She was so pure… He kept her in ignorance so she wouldn’t know the difference between right and wrong.

At night, he’d stop in front of her bedroom door and just… wait. Letting the fear build, the sick fuck. Then either he’d leave, or he’d go in. And when he went in, he’d raise a dome to muffle every sound. Liora, her mother, knew nothing. Nobody did, though Sparda had his doubts, he couldn’t accuse him without proof. Ironically, Liora was too scared to stand up to her husband, thinking he was just strict and that opposing him would make it worse. Tragic, right?

Me…(clenches his fists, voice hoarse) I was just a kid. All I thought about was running around, having fun, fighting with Vergil. I saw nothing. Noticed nothing. And fuck, I still hate myself for it. Vergil, though, he felt everything through their “soulbound”. He suspected she was being beaten, he could sense her fear, her pain… but he couldn’t put the pieces together or find any proof. He blamed himself too, you know.

(He lifts his head, a bitter smile slowly returning.)
But at least my brother did what needed to be done. Years later… after the house burned and Mom… (sigh) [the rest of the bio in the comments ⬇️]
